The institution's own mission page (https://dev.friart.ch/en/about/mission) and e-flux (https://www.e-flux.com/directory/217250/kunsthalle-friart-fribourg) say it was founded in 1981. An archive page on friart.ch (https://friart.ch/en/archives/focus/the-struggle-to-obtain-a-space) says the Fri Art story began in 1979 with the founding of a non-profit organisation. The first big event, Fri Art 81, took place in the old diocesan seminary two years later. The association had no premises for about ten years. They were granted in November 1990, and the building at Petites-Rames 22 was inaugurated in 1991. Address: the official site writes the postcode as 1701. MySwitzerland lists Petites-Rames 22, 1700 Fribourg, and museums.ch lists Kleinrahmengasse 22 in its contact block, which looks like the German form of the same street.

b.year_basis: 'Founded in 1981' per the institution's own site and the Fribourg regional tourism page
b.year_statement: The institution's own site and the Fribourg regional tourism page both give 1981 as the founding year, and describe it as a venue for contemporary art on the French/German language border in Switzerland (the central institution for contemporary art on the border between French and German-speaking Switzerland. Founded in 1981).
b.address: Petites-Rames 22, CP 294, CH–1701 Fribourg
b.address_statement: The address appears as Kunsthalle Friart Fribourg, Petites-Rames 22, CP 294, CH–1701 Fribourg.
b.notes: Art Rabbit traces the story to 1979, when Michel Ritter and a group of artists founded a non-profit organisation called Fri Art, with the large exhibition Fri Art 81 following; the institution's own pages say founded 1981, which is used here. In 1991 it moved into the industrial building at Petites-Rames 22 (so 1991 is a move, not the founding). CP 294 is the postal box as the official site writes it. museums.ch lists the German form Kleinrahmengasse 22 for the same street number.

a.address_statement: Kunsthaus Hamburg is at Klosterwall 15, 20095 Hamburg.
a.notes: Two events are stated: founded 1962, opened to the public the following year (1963). 1962 is given as the founding year; use 1963 if the database wants the public opening. The first building (Paul Seitz, Ferdinandstor) was demolished in the early 1990s and the institution moved in 1993 to the former flower market hall at the current address, which it shares with other cultural institutions; the address given is the current one. Not the Hamburger Kunsthalle, a separate and older museum. Official site pages (kunsthaushamburg.de) were used for both values.

a.year_basis: founded (the Vienna Secession association of artists, 3 April 1897)
a.year_statement: The Vienna Secession was an art movement founded in 1897 by a group of artists who broke away from the city's established art association. Sources agree on the founding date of 3 April 1897.
a.address: Friedrichstraße 12, 1010 Vienna, Austria
a.address_statement: Address Friedrichstraße 12, 1010 Vienna, Austria
a.notes: Secession is the artists' association founded in 1897 and also its exhibition building; the building was completed in 1898 (Joseph Maria Olbrich), which is a different event and not used for the year. The address comes from third-party listings (structurae, museumforall). The official page https://secession.at/building appeared in the results, but the quoted text there only says the site was on Friedrichstraße, so it is not cited for the house number. Not to be confused with Hotel Secession at Getreidemarkt 5, 1060 Vienna, which is a separate business.

b.year_basis: founded (the association was founded on 3 April 1897 by Klimt, Moser, Hoffmann, Olbrich, Kurzweil, Bernatzik and others); the exhibition building was completed and the first exhibition held in 1898
b.year_statement: The Vienna Secession was founded on 3 April 1897 by artists Gustav Klimt, Koloman Moser, Josef Hoffmann, Joseph Maria Olbrich, Max Kurzweil, Wilhelm Bernatzik and others.
b.address: Friedrichstraße 12, 1010 Vienna, Austria
b.address_statement: Secession, Friedrichstraße 12, 1010 Vienna, Austria.
b.notes: Name clash: 'Secession' also means the wider art movement (Sezessionstil), and Hotel Secession in Vienna is a separate hotel. The record is the artists' association and its exhibition building. The year is for the association's founding, not the building, which was completed in 1898. Sources disagree on the first president, on Klimt versus Rudolf von Alt, and on whether Otto Wagner was an original founder. They do not disagree on 1897. The search text did not say which Links entry carried the address sentence, so the official secession.at page and an e-flux listing are both given. The summary also said the phone number differs between a travel listing and e-flux.
